challenge.method: Read §4(b) with the §4 opening and §0 definitions. Tested whether §4(d)(1) displaces §4(b), whether §3 narrows §4(b) to particular header material, and whether §6 elections or the GPLv3 control's §§7 and 14 change the meaning of §4(b) in the cited edition.
challenge.results: No material contradiction. Section 4(d)(1) offers a way to satisfy §4(d) using a runtime copy already on the user's system and a mechanism that works with an interface-compatible modified Library. Section 4(b) remains a separate condition. Section 3 has its own notice and two-copy conditions when the incorporated header material exceeds its listed exceptions. Section 6 can permit a different edition to be chosen depending on the Library's terms. The GPLv3 control provisions address additional permissions and GPL version elections, consistent with reading the two-copy condition under LGPLv3 as written.

limitations: Section 4(b) specifies the documents to supply and leaves filenames unspecified. A filename recommendation is a separate matter.
The review establishes one condition of §4. Which edition governs a particular work and whether a concrete distribution satisfies all applicable conditions require separate assessment.

The GPLv3 control establishes edition identity from the GCC release excerpt. The installer representation was outside the evidence inspected. The complete LGPL v3 digest was compared as reported by the tool, and the designated ranges were independently hashed.
reasoning: The §4 opening makes the listed requirements conditions of conveying a Combined Work under that section. Section 4(b) requires accompanying copies of both documents. Section 0 identifies those documents as GNU LGPL version 3 and GNU GPL version 3, and defines a Combined Work as a work produced by combining or linking an Application with the Library. The recomputed claim SHA-256 matches the requested revision.
